**CITES NOTHING, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS AN APPLICATION OF TODAY'S FINDING RATHER THAN AN OMISSION (vc 2026-08-20 16:22Z).** `11762943` ruled that a `to-write` row may cite a path or nothing and must not be forced to invent one. **Three rows today carried citations that had expired or were wrong, and every one was caught by a builder trying to satisfy the row rather than by any instrument here** -- `at lint` exempts `to-write` from L2 and L3, correctly, so a citation cannot be validated until somebody uses it. **A path invented now is a claim nothing will check until it is already wrong.** The builder names the file when the file exists.

**WHAT THIS ROW MUST ASSERT, AND THE CONTROL IT NEEDS.** Each of the four collection URLs resolves through `address::parse` and through the one resolution function, driven rather than asserted from the enum. **The denominator must come from D57-8's amended fence, not from `address.rs`** -- a denominator read out of the implementation agrees with it by construction, which is exactly how the nine-form list went four short without anyone noticing. **AND THE RED-FIRST ARM MUST BE THE FOURTH FORM SPECIFICALLY:** `Threads`, `Issues` and `WpCollection` are the POST clause's three and would be reached by any test written from that clause alone; `AcCollection` comes from the under-addressing clause and is the one a builder sourcing from the obvious paragraph will miss. **A test that passes without it has reproduced the original defect one level down.**

**NOT A WIDENING OF AT-07.1 AND `d57_8_forms()` IS NOT THE HOME FOR IT.** That helper is AT-07.1's denominator over entity forms; growing it to thirteen would silently move AC-07.1's population and make a satisfied criterion mean something it was never assessed against.

**BUILT AND GREENED 2026-08-21 (ic). `native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/tests/address_collections_resolve.rs`, 2 tests, driven at HEAD `510d4b10` on a tree clean but for this row's own work.**

**THE DENOMINATOR IS READ FROM CANON AND NOTHING IS HAND-COPIED.** The test loads `intent/.canon/st/ST0057.json` as a typed `Thread`, takes `design.md`'s attachment `text`, bounds the `## D57-8` section at the next same-level heading, asserts it carries EXACTLY TWO fences, and takes the second. Canon's recorded `sha256` is cross-checked against the disk file when it is present -- measured equal at `abc9a205...`, 33538 bytes both sides -- and an ABSENT disk file is not a divergence, which is what makes the row survive dehydration. Every failure path is a refusal naming what it could not find. **`d57_8_forms()` was NOT touched, so AC-07.1's population has not moved.**

**RED-FIRST, AND IT IS A PAIR RATHER THAN ONE PLANTED BREAK.** Mutation: `AcCollection`'s parse arm deleted from `address.rs:449`. Results, all four from one run:

| test | property | under mutation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AT-07.7 `every_d57_8_collection_form_resolves` | the four collections resolve | **RED** -- `intent:///threads/ST0056/ac ... has trailing segments after a complete address` |
| throwaway POST-clause-only control (3 forms) | Threads/Issues/WpCollection resolve | GREEN |
| AT-07.1 `every_d57_8_form_resolves` | the nine ENTITY forms resolve | GREEN |
| AT-07.1 `a_short_address_is_reported_as_short_and_never_as_trailing` | prefix diagnostics | RED (unforeseen) |

**The control staying green is the half that matters: a test sourced from D57-8's POST clause alone passes while `AcCollection` is broken**, so the under-addressing clause's form is load-bearing and this row has not reproduced the original defect one level down.

**THE UNFORESEEN RED IS REPORTED BECAUSE IT SHARPENS THE ROW RATHER THAN BECAUSE IT WAS EXPECTED.** AT-07.1's prefix test derives its population by truncating `d57_8_forms()` -- a THIRD consumer of that list, beside the coverage and round-trip rows -- so `intent:///threads/ST0056/ac`, a proper prefix of the `Ac` form, is already in its population. **But its arm for that case is literally `Ok(_) => {}`, an EMPTY arm.** Its doc comment names `/threads/<id>/ac` as a collection that is an entity in its own right and then asserts only that it does not refuse-as-trailing. **A URL resolving to the WRONG entity passes it unread.** So AT-07.1 touches this address and asserts nothing about it, which is the vacuous green this thread keeps paying for, and it is exactly the ground this row now covers: resolution to a named entity, round trip, format-independence, distinctness, and a stated population.

**THE STRUCTURAL ARM IS FORM-DEPENDENT ON PURPOSE, AND THERE IS NO SECOND SCHEME SCAN.** `no_second_resolver_exists` asks *does any other crate spell the scheme*, which is form-INDEPENDENT and therefore already covers these four; writing another would be the Highlander defect, and the lift of `collect_scheme_hits` into `tests/common/` proposed on 2026-08-20 was WITHDRAWN rather than granted -- AT-07.1's file is untouched. What this row adds instead is the arm a scheme scan cannot make: an exhaustive `match` over `Entity`, so a fourteenth variant does not COMPILE until somebody classifies it. The dependency on the sibling's singularity arm is pinned by name rather than left as a comment, because a contract half-held in another file can be deleted without this row noticing; it checks a NAME, which is the wrong instrument for a capability question and the right one here, since a rename fails loudly and the hazard guarded is silent removal.

**SCOPE RULED BY hv 2026-08-21 ON ic's ESCALATION: this row is built to its BODY -- parse and resolve -- and not to representation.** `view_path_of`'s wildcard, found while researching this row, is a real defect and is being fixed SEPARATELY under AT-07.3 in `address.rs`, which is ic's. ic flagged the parse-only reading AGAINST ITSELF as the one that conveniently greens its own row; the resolution does more work rather than less, and stretches no row past its text.
